title: The adda that built modern India
excerpt: In a coffee house in Kolkata, the same conversations have been happening since 1942. The regulars say nothing important has changed.
body:
Indian Coffee House on College Street is not remarkable to look at. The walls are the yellow of old turmeric. What is remarkable is that this room produced arguments that shaped the Indian republic. Tagore debated here. Mrinal Sen planned films here.

The practice is called adda — the Kolkata tradition of purposeless, passionate conversation. It has no agenda. There is no conclusion. The point is to think out loud in the company of people who will push back.

"Adda is not gossip," Subrata Mukhopadhyay, a retired professor, tells me firmly. "Gossip is about people. Adda is about ideas. The moment you start talking about who said what about whom, it is over."
